title: Andersen–Haboush trivial Frobenius pushforward at rho weights
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and with every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group having finite central kernel an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ (a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup), with character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$ and integer coroot pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Here a split maximal torus is a maximal subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$. Write $p:B\to T$ for the projection with kernel the unipotent radical and put $Q=S/B$. For $\mu\in X$ put $\widetilde\mu=\mu\circ p$ and $M_\mu=\mathcal L_{-\widetilde\mu}$ [lem-sfb-homogeneous-line-bundle-sections], the invertible sheaf associated to the quotient action $(g,z)\cdot b=(gb,\widetilde\mu(b)z)$. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$, the actual character supplied by [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Assume $\operatorname{char}F=p_0>0$ (so $p_0$ is prime). Let $\operatorname{Fr}_Q:Q\to Q$ be absolute Frobenius: the identity on points and the $p_0$-power map on regular functions [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]. For every integer $r\ge1$ put $q=p_0^r$ and $f_r=\operatorname{Fr}_Q^r$. Then $f_r$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and there is an integer $d_r\ge1$ and an isomorphism of Zariski $\mathcal O_Q$-modules $$ (f_r)_*M_{(q-1)\rho}\simeq\mathcal O_Q^{\oplus d_r}. $$ Pushforward has the scalar action through $f_r^\sharp$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; no $F$-linearity of the absolute Frobenius is asserted. The isomorphism is an ordinary module isomorphism, with no equivariance requirement. The statement includes $S=1$, in which case $d_r=1$.

source.place: Part II, 4.4--4.5, Andersen–Haboush Frobenius argument, WANTED. Online corroboration read: Mathieu, Tilting Modules and their Applications, AS Pure Math 26 (2000), Lemma 3.1, printed p.157, https://www.imsc.res.in/~knr/vdk/mathieu.pdf; Thomsen, Flag varieties, Toric varieties and characteristic p geometry (1998), Part I Theorem 5.1, printed p.27, https://pure.au.dk/ws/files/428868227/imf_phd_1998_jft.pdf. The formula is stated here for iterated absolute Frobenius, forgetting linearizations and the dimension formula.

proof.text: Write $p=p_0$ and put $N=|\Phi^+|$. The Bruhat-chart statement gives an integral $Q$ covered by opens isomorphic to $\mathbf A_F^N$, on each of which $M_\mu$ is trivial because the $B$-torsor has a section. Since $F$ is algebraically closed, every coefficient has a unique $p^r$th root. On such a chart the monomials $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_N^{a_N}$, $0\le a_i<p^r$, form a basis of $F[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ over its subring of $p^r$th powers: write each exponent uniquely as $p^r b_i+a_i$ and take roots of coefficients. Thus every $f_r$ is finite, and $(f_r)_*M_\mu$ is locally free of rank $p^{rN}$. The calculation localizes by replacing a denominator $s$ with $s^{p^r}$; these define the same open. This proves the finiteness clause directly, without a flat-Frobenius theorem.

proof.text: Put $\eta=(p-1)\rho$, $V=\Gamma(Q,M_\eta)$, $\mathfrak u=\operatorname{Lie}(U)$ and $A=u(\mathfrak u)$. The rho-orbit statement gives $-w_0\eta=\eta$ and $\langle\eta,\alpha^\vee\rangle=p-1$. The restricted-induced-invariants lemma therefore gives $V^{\mathfrak u}=Fv_+$ with $v_+\ne0$. The restricted-freeness lemma gives $V^\vee\simeq u(\operatorname{Lie}(U^-))$. Conjugation by $n_0$ identifies this restricted algebra with $A$: conjugation takes invariant derivations to invariant derivations and commutes with their $p$th iterates. The PBW-dimension statement now gives $\dim_F V=\dim_F V^\vee=\dim_F A=p^N$. This dimension argument uses neither the induced Weyl dimension formula nor Kempf vanishing.

proof.text:
Let $R=\mathcal O_Q^p\subseteq\mathcal O_Q$, the image sheaf of the $p$-power map. By integrality, $a\mapsto a^p$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings $\mathcal O_Q\to R$, though not generally over $F$. Since $F$ is perfect, its constants belong to $R$. Regard $M=M_\eta$ as an $R$-module and form
$$\theta:R\otimes_F V\longrightarrow M,\qquad a\otimes v\longmapsto av.$$
Under the ring-sheaf isomorphism $\mathcal O_Q\to R$, the target is precisely $\operatorname{Fr}_{Q*}M$ with the scalar action in the statement, and the source is free of rank $p^N$. The infinitesimal action on $M$ comes from its homogeneous linearization. It is $R$-linear because a derivation kills every $p$th power; on the source it acts only on $V$. The product rule $x(av)=x(a)v+a(xv)=a(xv)$ proves that $\theta$ is $A$-linear. These are sheaf actions: infinitesimal translations are the identity on the underlying topological space, so act over every open.

proof.text:
The augmentation ideal $J\subset A$ has $J^h=0$. At any stalk, if $K=\ker\theta$ were nonzero, choose the largest $j$ with $J^jK\ne0$; then $J^jK$ contains a nonzero element killed by $J$. But
$$(R\otimes_F V)^{\mathfrak u}=R\otimes_F V^{\mathfrak u}=Rv_+.$$
Indeed choose a finite basis of $\mathfrak u$ and express all its operators as one matrix over $F$; row reduction puts its common kernel into coordinate form and the same invertible row and column operations work over every $F$-algebra, including each stalk of $R$. On $Rv_+$, $\theta$ is multiplication by the nonzero section $v_+$. The Bruhat charts give an integral $Q$, so every local frame writes this section as a nonzero element of a domain; its germ is nonzero at every point and multiplication is injective. Thus $K=0$ at every stalk and $\theta$ is injective.

source.place: Section 3, Lemma 3.1, printed p.157, and the iteration in Theorem 3.2, printed pp.157--158; WANTED locally; read online https://www.imsc.res.in/~knr/vdk/mathieu.pdf. Agent expansion over the p-power subsheaf, with the source conventions L(-lambda)=M_lambda.

proof.text: Step 1 gives both sides of $\theta$ the same finite rank over $R$. At the generic point the injective map is an isomorphism, so in local frames its determinant is nonzero and it is invertible on a nonempty open. Its invertibility locus is open, since the inverse matrix is adjugate divided by determinant. For each $g\in S(F)$, translation preserves $R$ and sends $\theta(a\otimes v)$ to $\theta((ga)\otimes(gv))$; hence that open is $S(F)$-stable. The $B$-torsor gives transitivity on $Q(F)$: the fibre over an $F$-point is nonempty of finite type and has an $F$-point by the affine Nullstellensatz. The nonempty open also has an $F$-point, by taking an affine part of a Bruhat chart and the same Nullstellensatz. It therefore contains all $Q(F)$. Every closed point is an $F$-point, again affine-locally by Nullstellensatz. If the complementary closed subset were nonempty, the Jacobson-density statement would give a closed point in it, a contradiction. Thus $\theta$ is everywhere invertible. Transport through $\mathcal O_Q\simeq R$ gives $\operatorname{Fr}_{Q*}M_{(p-1)\rho}\simeq\mathcal O_Q^{\oplus p^N}$.

proof.text:
Write $L=M_\rho$. The character multiplication in the associated-bundle construction gives $M_{m\rho}\simeq L^{\otimes m}$ for $m\ge0$: tensoring the local frames multiplies their transition characters. For any invertible sheaf $P$ in characteristic $p$, absolute Frobenius pullback raises its transition functions to their $p$th powers, so $\operatorname{Fr}_Q^*P\simeq P^{\otimes p}$. The ordinary projection formula with an invertible $P$ is verified in a local frame $e$: the map $\operatorname{Fr}_*M\otimes P\to\operatorname{Fr}_*(M\otimes\operatorname{Fr}^*P)$ sends $m\otimes e$ to $m\otimes\operatorname{Fr}^*e$; replacing $e$ by $ue$ multiplies the right frame by $u^p$, exactly the scalar action on $\operatorname{Fr}_*M$. Thus the local isomorphisms glue. For $r\ge2$, the identity $p^r-1=(p-1)+p(p^{r-1}-1)$ and step 5 now give
$$\operatorname{Fr}_*M_{(p^r-1)\rho}\simeq M_{(p^{r-1}-1)\rho}^{\oplus p^N}.$$
Apply $(\operatorname{Fr}^{r-1})_*$, which preserves finite direct sums sectionwise. Starting from step 5, induction yields $(f_r)_*M_{(p^r-1)\rho}\simeq\mathcal O_Q^{\oplus p^{rN}}$. Set $d_r=p^{rN}\ge1$. When $S=1$, $N=0$, $Q=\operatorname{Spec}F$, and the same calculation gives $d_r=1$, with the ring isomorphism $a\mapsto a^{p^r}$ supplying the scalar transport.
